strengths: The no-block contract is explicit in both operator docs and installed skill guidance: dirty or hard runtime windows are scoped and do not automatically suppress unrelated clean-window work.

Approval is conservative: only strict PATCH_CANDIDATE rows with repeat evidence, documented VisionAI surface, low-risk file targets, clean runtime scope, and an approved operation become auto-approved.
PATCH_PROPOSAL is clearly treated as concrete read-only configuration work, not runtime apply authority.
Guarded apply is split into approval, fake apply, and real apply, with fake apply required before real apply.

Invalid packages fail closed before writer invocation for stale fingerprints, manual-review changes, blocked changes, missing approved operations, unsafe target files, aggregate CardBehavior.json, symlinks, invalid deck slugs, nested runtime paths, unsupported special files, and GameCardId mismatches.
The apply path writes post_apply_validation_handoff.json after real apply, forcing fresh validation games before gameplay-improvement claims.

Operator summary exposes non-patch work queues, including review, parser work, contract-gap work, runtime work, never-autopatch work, and identity/decision-trace work, which reduces false no-signal outcomes.

Focused regression coverage directly tests valid clean candidate flow, dirty candidate blocking, unrelated hard runtime failures allowing partial preview, same-window hard failures blocking, stale freshness blocking, and invalid package blocking.
The skill file is short and operationally usable: it points to authoritative docs, keeps command order compact, and avoids embedding a large HSTuner-style scope.
gaps: No actual property-based test framework coverage was found; the requested property-test dimension is covered by deterministic unit/integration tests, not Hypothesis-style generative properties.

Full unittest discovery could not be completed during this audit because python -m unittest discover -v became quiet/hung after initial acceptance tests and was terminated. Focused gate coverage passed, but full-suite pass is [uncertain].

The approval gate depends on artifacts already encoding correct clean-window and candidate scope. The gate is fail-closed when that proof is missing, but this audit did not replay a live analyze-step2 run end to end from fresh HearthRanger/HDT evidence.

The installed skill is slim, but it still references many operator artifacts and commands; the docs are necessary for correctness, yet a new operator could still need the README and operator docs to understand all boundary details.

Hearthstone mechanic coverage is broad in docs and operator summary vocabulary, but this audit focused on no-block/apply behavior rather than proving every modern Wild mechanic with fresh live examples.
no_block_assessment: Valid decks or Step 2 runs with warning-only or unrelated blocked areas can proceed as visible work: docs/operator/semantic-coverage.md:26 and docs/operator/README.md:154 state row/window scoping, and tests/test_blocker_summary.py:324 plus tests/test_blocker_summary.py:1445 verify partial preview is still allowed when hard/non-hard failures are outside the promoted candidate scope.

Valid clean strict candidates can proceed through approval and guarded apply: tests/test_approved_patch_bundle.py:13 produces APPROVED_PATCH_BUNDLE_READY and tests/test_guarded_auto_apply_e2e.py:15 proves the approve, fake apply, apply, and post-apply handoff path.

Warning and review-only surfaces do not silently become auto-apply authority: tests/test_approved_patch_bundle.py covers manual-review flags, review-only patchability, target uncertainty, GlobalValues, generated entities, secrets, aura ambiguity, random discard ambiguity, and single-event broad GlobalValues as blocked or manual-review rather than approved.

Invalid packages still block: src/hsranger_core/apply_approved_patch.py:127 validates bundle readiness and fingerprints, while src/hsranger_core/apply_approved_patch.py:271 and :402 validate runtime/package shape before writer invocation; tests/test_apply_approved_patch.py:100 and :159 verify these blocks.

Technical hard-block behavior is appropriately scoped: a hard runtime failure touching a promoted candidate blocks partial preview, an unrelated hard failure can allow partial preview, unknown or unscoped hard failures block conservatively, and false parser capabilities only block when referenced by active rows.

The current contract is not a blanket no-block policy. It is a scoped no-block policy: warnings, non-hard failures, irrelevant semantic families, and unrelated dirty windows do not globally block, but stale evidence, unknown runtime scope, touched hard failures, invalid runtime files, unsafe operations, and manual-review surfaces still block.
skill_slimness_assessment: The repo skill at skills/hearthranger-config/SKILL.md is concise for the amount of workflow it controls: it lists required inputs, authoritative docs, command order, Step 2 command shape, and report checklist without embedding large implementation logic.
It is autonomous enough for Codex operation because it states exact command order, exact artifacts to read first, and exact readiness/status labels.

It is efficient because the skill delegates detail to docs/operator/README.md, docs/operator/new-deck-checklist.md, docs/operator/guarded-auto-apply.md, and references/post-run-finetuning.md instead of duplicating all content.
It is not overloaded with HSTuner scope in the inspected file; it stays focused on hsranger-core, HearthRanger runtime writes, Step 2 analysis, guarded apply, and validation handoff.
Slimness is good enough rather than optimal because the report checklist is still dense and includes many artifact names; a one-page quick decision tree could further reduce operator load.
hearthstone_coverage_assessment: Pre-run runtime package surfaces are represented in the workflow through Mulligan.json, GlobalValues.json, per-card CardID JSON files, Combo.json handling, config preview reports, syntax reports, and guarded write receipts.

The apply gate intentionally allows only low-risk per-card CardBehavior append rows and simple Mulligan append rows for auto-apply; GlobalValues and Combo surfaces are manual-review or unsupported for automatic mutation, which is conservative and appropriate for broad/high-impact mechanics.
Hero Power and weapon semantics are treated cautiously: approval marks unclear weapon or hero-power semantics for manual review unless action semantics are clear.

Modern and Wild mechanic families are visible in operator summary and never-autopatch handling, including generated_entity, aura_ongoing, secret, discard, deathrattle, reborn, recruit, summon_from_deck, discover, dredge, tradeable, overload, freeze, lifesteal, taunt, rush, charge, positioning, location, weapon, weapon_attack, hero_power_swap, destroy, silence, transform, resurrection_resolution, and lethal_setup.

Generated entities, hidden secrets, unclear aura causality, random discard without discarded-card identity, discover/dredge without option payloads, target uncertainty, and broad single-event GlobalValues are warning/manual-review/never-autopatch cases rather than auto-applied changes.
Coverage depth is right for the no-block/apply boundary: the system surfaces mechanic work and review queues without pretending every mechanic is safe to patch automatically.
This audit did not prove every listed mechanic against fresh live HearthRanger/HDT samples, so full live mechanic coverage remains [uncertain].
